# dsh-orchestrator
Spawn, prompt and track agent chats and tasks from one Orchestrate tab, with orch_* tools and runner

**Agent swarm + task orchestration for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).**
A plugin that adds an **Orchestrate** tab to dsh-better-sidebar, like the built-in Background Tasks
an **Orchestrate** tab to dsh-better-sidebar, like the built-in Background Tasks view, but broader:
- **Agents**: create, list, prompt, **fork** (split a conversation), fan-out and cancel agent chats,

with a **chat-style** transcript drawer. Sessions address all of it through 14 `orch_*` tools.
- **
Tasks**: tracked, status-updated work of four kinds: `command` (shell on any runner), `scrape` (dete
rministic multi-URL extraction, no model in the loop), `http` (endpoint calls), `agent` (a spawned c

hat whose answer is the task output).
- **Runners**: where commands execute: this host, ssh targets,
or remote **tool servers** (any other host running this plugin). Explicit selection or the configur

ed default.
- **Providers**: external integrations rendered as status cards, including an optional H

PC allocation card and any JSON status endpoint.
- **Remote API**: a secret-protected machine API: p
rompt chats, spawn agents, create tasks, and serve the tool-server contract so OTHER hosts can run w
ts, spawn agents, create tasks, and serve the tool-server contract so OTHER hosts can run work here.
Everything is **settings-driven**: runners, providers, presets, limits and the API secret live in Se
ttings → Orchestrator (or the cordis config row). Nothing is hardcoded, no hosts, no commands, no cr
edentials in the code.

## Install
Requires DSH >= 0.1.1-rc.1, Node >= 22.5, the `web` profile, and dsh-better-sidebar (the tab host).
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator`, or from GitHub: `dsh
plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-orchestrator`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`lib/` is committed, so no build step is needed. Then **restart dsh-web** (the client half mounts li
ve after a browser refresh; the host half, tools, settings namespace, API route, needs the restart).
Full steps are in cordis.patch.yml.
## The tab
Open the sidebar **+** menu → **Orchestrate**. Five sections:
| Section | What it shows / does |
| **agents** | every chat (live + cold) with title, running state, recency; quick **prompt**, **stop
**, **chat** drawer (transcript + send box + fork + cancel); **+ new agent** spawn form with fan-out

|
| **tasks** | every task with status, runner, live output (auto-polling while running), cancel; *

*+ new task** form for all four types |
| **runners** | execution targets with health probes |
| **p
roviders** | integration cards, an hpc provider shows the allocation headline, queue, collector heal

th and staged proposals |
| **api** | machine-API secret management + ready-made curl examples + the
tool-server contract |
A badge on the tab counts active work (running agents + running tasks).
## The agent tools
Sessions get these tools (registered through the standard `ctx.tools` seam, they behave like any cor

| tool | what it does |

| `orch_status` | one-screen overview: agents, tasks by status, runners, providers |
| `orch_agents_

list` | list chats (live/cold, titles, running flags), with search |
| `orch_agent_status` | one cha

t: running state + last user/assistant text |
| `orch_agent_prompt` | deliver a message into a chat

(id, unique prefix, or exact title); cold chats resume |
| `orch_agent_spawn` | create chat(s), opti
onally with a first prompt; `count` fans out with `{i}` interpolation, **how you split work across a

gents** |
| `orch_agent_fork` | **split a conversation**: fork a chat's completed-turn history into

a new session, then prompt the fork |
| `orch_agent_cancel` | cancel a chat's active turn (queued wo

rk is kept) |
| `orch_task_create` | create + run a task (see below) |
| `orch_task_list` / `orch_ta

sk_status` / `orch_task_output` | list / inspect / read tasks |
| `orch_task_cancel` | cancel a task

(kills the runner process or cancels the agent turn) |
| `orch_runners` | runner inventory + health

probes |
| `orch_providers` | provider status cards (for example an HPC allocation) |
## Task types
| type | spec fields | output |

| `command` | `command`, `cwd`, `runner`, `timeoutMs` | stdout + stderr, capped |
| `scrape` | `urls
[]`, `extract` (text/html/json), `selector` (tag/.class/#id/[attr]), `attribute`, `pattern` (regex)

| JSON rows: per-URL status + extracted data |
| `http` | `url`, `method`, `body`, `headers`, `expec

tStatus`, `timeoutMs` | response body, capped |

## Security model
Two caller classes, two gates (full detail in docs/DESIGN.md):
- **Browser** (tab + settings UI): loopback peer + trust fence (Host authority, no cross-site) on re
ads; adds same-origin `sec-fetch-site`/Origin, JSON content-type, the plugin's `X-Requested-With` he

ader, and the harness session cookie presence on mutations. No GET ever mutates.
- **Machine** (curl
/ cron / other boxes): the operator secret, constant-time compared, per-IP rate-limited, with a tig

hter wrong-secret budget. Fails closed with no secret.
- Commands run with a **scrubbed environment*
* (PATH/HOME/LANG only) and argv-only spawning. SSH credentials are the operator's ssh config; http
tokens are env vars read at call time. Secrets never appear in settings reads, logs, or the task sto
ens are env vars read at call time. Secrets never appear in settings reads, logs, or the task store.
